Look-alike colors, line patterns and turn positions from the curb, lane and turning pages, each tied to one handbook page; hint metadata sits only in the trailing line of a block.

FACT_ID: sec13-R01 | anchor: A01
A white curb allows a brief stop for passengers, a yellow curb allows a brief stop for loading while you stay with the car, and a red curb allows no stop at all. [A01]
Why it matters: group curb colors; difficulty two; confusable sec13-F01 versus sec13-F02 versus sec13-F03.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec13-R02 | anchor: A01
A broken white line may be crossed after signaling when safe, while a double solid white line may not be crossed. [A01]
Why it matters: group white lines; difficulty two; confusable sec13-F08 versus sec13-F12.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec13-R03 | anchor: A01
The solid white right-edge line is crossed only for an emergency or a road hazard, while a solid white line beside an HOV lane may be crossed to merge in or out. [A01]
Why it matters: group white lines; difficulty three; confusable sec13-F10 versus sec13-F11.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec13-R04 | anchor: A01
White lane lines divide traffic going the same way, while yellow lane lines divide traffic going opposite ways. [A01]
Why it matters: group line colors; difficulty one; confusable sec13-F06 versus sec13-F13.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec13-R05 | anchor: A01
A single white line can mark the right pavement edge, while a single yellow line can mark the left pavement edge on divided highways and one-way streets. [A01]
Why it matters: group edge lines; difficulty three; confusable sec13-F07 versus sec13-F14.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec13-R06 | anchor: A01
Double dashed yellow lines usually signal a reversible lane, whose direction depends on the time of day. [A01]
Why it matters: group reversible lanes; difficulty two; prereq sec13-F15.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec13-R07 | anchor: A01
On a long one-way street the center lane is preferred because the outer lanes serve turning vehicles. [A01]
Why it matters: group lane choice; difficulty one; prereq sec13-F04.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec13-R08 | anchor: A02
Turning right on red needs a full stop before the crosswalk, while turning left on red is allowed only from a one-way road onto another one-way road. [A02]
Why it matters: group turns on red; difficulty three; confusable sec13-F24 versus sec13-F32.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec13-R09 | anchor: A02
A left turn from a two-way road starts in the lane just right of the center line, while a left turn from a one-way road starts in the lane nearest the left curb. [A02]
Why it matters: group left-turn positions; difficulty three; confusable sec13-F28 versus sec13-F34.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec13-R10 | anchor: A02
A right turn normally ends in the right lane of the new road, while a left turn onto a one-way road ends in its far left lane. [A02]
Why it matters: group turn endings; difficulty two; confusable sec13-F27 versus sec13-F33.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec13-R11 | anchor: A02
A marked left-turn lane must be used for a left turn, while turns from more than one lane are allowed only where signs and markings show it. [A02]
Why it matters: group turn lanes; difficulty two; confusable sec13-F30 versus sec13-F21.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0047]
